report:
## Bottom line

- **Policy (part 1):** Anthropic's help center says `claude -p` and the Agent SDK, when signed in with a plan, draw from that plan's own 5-hour and weekly limits (updates dated Oct 7 and June 15, 2026). The consumer terms still bar automated access unless it goes through an API key or Anthropic explicitly permits it. Routing a plan login through a third-party harness is the category at risk: the Claude Code legal page already forbids it, and a Usage Policy clause effective Nov 12, 2026 names it.
- **Issue #97074 (part 2):** I found no Anthropic staff reply in the parts of the thread I could read (through Nov 2). The only Anthropic-side statement is a general X post by Boris Cherny (Oct 28) that does not mention `sdk-cli`. `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` is not in the official env-var pages I could read, and no Anthropic text I read endorses or forbids overriding it. The effect is community-measured only.
- **Mechanisms (part 3):** Channels are a research preview for Pro, Max and Ultra: an MCP server pushes events in and a reply tool sends results out. Remote Control (Pro, Max, Ultra; Team and Enterprise need an admin) is a human-driven window with no documented input API for scripts. Hooks (Stop, SubagentStop, Notification) are outbound only. Agent view and `claude --bg` are a research preview, read through `claude agents --json` and `claude logs`. Agent teams are experimental and interactive-only. `--session-id` and `--resume` are documented. `statusline` `rate_limits` is documented for Pro, Max and Ultra. `/usage` is documented but not scriptable. The OAuth usage endpoint is undocumented. The only documented same-machine way for a script to post into a running interactive session is the cross-session inbox socket.

## 1. What the policy documents say

### 1.1 Help center: Use the Claude Agent SDK with your Claude plan

My fetch returned only the two dated update notices, not the article body. The notices are the operative text:

- **Oct 7, 2026:** Max, Ultra and Team plans include monthly API credits covering the Claude API, Managed Agents, the Agent SDK and `claude -p`, but only “when you run them with an API key from your linked Claude Console organization.” It adds: “Nothing changes for your plan: when you’re signed in with your Claude plan, the Claude Agent SDK and claude -p still draw from your subscription limits.”
- **June 15, 2026:** “We’ve paused the previously-announced changes to Claude Agent SDK usage. For now, nothing has changed: Claude Agent SDK, claude -p, and third-party app usage still draw from your subscription’s usage limits.”

Read together, these describe the mechanics: plan login means plan limits. They do not say that third-party harnesses are permitted. The June sentence is descriptive, not permissive.

The monthly-credits article adds the boundaries. Credits are $100 for Max, $200 for Ultra, and $20 or $100 per seat for Team (pooled, capped at $500). Pro is not eligible. The credits cover `claude -p` and the Agent SDK only when run with an API key from the linked Console organization. They do not cover interactive Claude Code, nor runs started by the Claude Code GitHub Action, the IDE extension or the desktop app, even with `-p`.

### 1.2 Consumer Terms of Service

The copy I read is dated Oct 8, 2025. It names Anthropic Ireland as the contracting entity and says it applies to consumers resident in the EEA or Switzerland. I did not read the US version.

- **Section 3:** Users may not access the Services “through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise,” except “when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it.”
- **Section 11 (“Non-commercial use only”):** No “commercial or business purposes.”
- **Section 2:** Users may not share login credentials or “make your Account available to anyone else.”
- **Section 4:** Users are responsible for all Actions taken on their behalf.
- **Preface:** The Commercial Terms govern API keys and the Console.

Reading: unattended automation through a subscription login sits outside the default permission. Anthropic's explicit permission for `claude -p` and the SDK is the help-center text plus the Legal page, not the Terms themselves. The Terms do not name `claude -p`, and “ordinary” use is not defined. Section 11 is a real constraint for business automation on a consumer plan.

### 1.3 Claude Code legal and compliance page

- The license split: Consumer Terms for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; Commercial Terms for Team, Enterprise and API users.
- “Advertised usage limits for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK.”
- OAuth is “intended exclusively for purchasers” of plans and “designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications.”
- Developers “including those using the Agent SDK, should use API key authentication.” Anthropic “does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, Max, or Ultra plan credentials on behalf of their users.” Developers “may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens.”
- Carve-out: an end user may still sign in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own subscription, even when a platform hosts Claude Code.
- Products that preinstall Claude Code must not modify the binary and may not resell or intermediate usage.

### 1.4 Agent SDK overview

“Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK.”

### 1.5 Usage Policy: the new clause

The policy page is marked effective Nov 12, 2026, so it is not yet in force (today is Nov 3). Under “Do Not Abuse Our Platform” it adds: “Resell, proxy, or otherwise provide access to Claude through unauthorized means, including services that route requests through consumer subscriptions or misrepresent the product or client being used.” A third-party tracker says the policy in force until Nov 11 contained no resale or proxy wording. I did not read that in-force text directly. The policy also says Anthropic may “throttle, limit, suspend, or terminate” access on suspicion of a violation.

### 1.6 What this means by route

- **Interactive Claude Code on your own machine** (channels, hooks, Remote Control, agent view): plan limits apply per the docs. These are Anthropic's own surfaces, not third-party harnesses. The Section 3 automation question remains open for unattended use.
- **`claude -p` or the SDK under your own login, for your own work:** Anthropic says it draws from plan limits. Business use conflicts with Section 11.
- **A third-party app that uses your plan login:** the Legal page forbids routing plan credentials for users. From Nov 12 the Usage Policy names this practice. This is the highest-risk category.
- **An API key from a linked Console organization (Max, Ultra, Team):** draws monthly credits and is governed by the Commercial Terms, not plan limits.

## 2. Issue anthropics/claude-code#97074

### 2.1 What the issue reports

Opened Sep 25, 2026 by qvarker (Claude Code 2.1.282, Opus 5, Linux). The reporter says the same tokens use about 1.8 times the 5-hour window headless (`entrypoint: sdk-cli`) versus the interactive TUI (`cli`). Labels: bug, area:cost, has-repro, api:anthropic. The thread has no assignee.

User-run replications, none verified by Anthropic:

- qvarker (Max, Opus 5): about $3.0 versus $1.6 per 1% of the window.
- Z3l20 (Pro, claude-opus-5-5, effort low, Sep 27): `sdk-cli` used $0.68 per 1%, the TUI $1.34, about 2.0 times.
- kler (Team, Claude Code 2.1.300, Oct 17): `sdk-ts` and `sdk-cli` drained about 2.8 to 3.0 times faster than a `claude-vscode` label. The harness set the labels, so this is a controlled but single-account result.
- futin (passive transcript audit, desktop app versus `sdk-cli`): 1.30 to 1.49 times.
- imnakul (Windows, uncontrolled, different tasks): headless about 22 to 24 points versus about 5 points for the CLI.

### 2.2 Has Anthropic responded?

- **GitHub:** In the thread I could read through Nov 2, there is no Anthropic staff comment. The page says “72 remaining items” and I could not load them. A direct request for an Anthropic answer is in the thread (imnakul, Oct 8; Ferfeit-style follow-ups through Nov 2 ask for one).
- **X (Boris Cherny, Oct 28, 11:51 PM UTC):** “We didn’t find a single root cause or any regression in Claude Code. In most cases, users who saw faster usage against limits were traced back to one or two heavy sessions (xhigh effort, /goal, Workflows, Agent Teams, long SDK jobs).” The post does not mention `sdk-cli`, headless runs or the entrypoint. An AICoder summary calls it a post by an employee, not a formal announcement.
- **Status as of Oct 31:** a DEV Community post says Anthropic had not confirmed the headless gap or announced a fix. That is the author's reading, and Theo of T3 Code had said he confirmed it as a bug on Anthropic's side.
- **Docs and changelog:** The costs, headless and CLI pages I read say nothing about weighting by entrypoint. The release notes I read (v2.1.310 to v2.1.316, Oct 23 to Oct 31) contain no entrypoint or metering change. I did not read the full changelog.
- **Feature request #99231** (Oct 3) asks for a documented read-only usage endpoint. It is open, and I saw no Anthropic reply.

### 2.3 Is the CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT override documented or discouraged?

**Documented?** Not in the official env-var page as far as I could read. My read of that page stopped before the `CLAUDE_CODE_E…` entries. Two third-party references say the variable is not in the official reference (turboai.dev). A third-party mirror generated from the binary lists it as set by the program when empty (`sdk-cli` for SDK CLI, `sdk-ts` for the TypeScript SDK), with an example `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli claude -p`. I could not confirm official status, so treat it as undocumented.

**Discouraged?** No Anthropic text I read discourages it. The nearest rules are the Usage Policy's “misrepresent the product or client being used” (effective Nov 12), which speaks directly to subscription routing, and the Legal page's rule that embedded Claude Code run “as published by Anthropic.” Neither addresses label overrides. Whether relabeling falls under the clause is unknown.

**Effect (community only):** The override changes the `cc_entrypoint` value sent with each request (in the `x-anthropic-billing-header` block, per the issue). T3 Code PR #25597 reports about 1.83 times more work per 1% after switching to a custom label (one Max account, Claude Code 2.1.310). A commenter on the same PR reports about 2.2 times on Windows. The PR is marked Closed on the page I read, and forks merged it. A known gap: an inherited `sdk-*` value keeps the default in place unless the override overwrites it. Anthropic has neither documented nor disavowed this.

## 3. The mechanisms

Status, plans and I/O below are from the official pages unless marked otherwise. “Label” means whether the docs say which entrypoint label the session uses. That matters because #97074 weights by label.

| Mechanism | Status | Plans (docs) | Message enters by | Output leaves by | Label documented? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Channels (MCP push) | Research preview | Pro, Max, Ultra: yes. Team and Enterprise: admin must enable. Console API key: allowed. Not on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry | MCP server pushes notifications into the open session; sender allowlist | Two-way: reply tool calls to the chat platform; no delivery acknowledgement | No |
| Remote Control | No preview label on the page; Trusted Devices is beta | Pro, Max, Ultra. Team and Enterprise: admin toggle. API keys not supported | Typed by the user in claude.ai/code or the Claude mobile app | Web and phone transcript, push notifications | No |
| Hooks: Stop, SubagentStop, Notification | No preview label; agent-based hooks are experimental | All providers | Hooks cannot start prompts | Hook stdout, exit code or JSON; `type: http` POST | n/a |
| Agent view and `claude --bg` | Research preview | Not in the feature table; no plan list found | `claude --bg "prompt"`, dispatch input, peek reply, `claude --resume <id> "prompt"` | `claude agents --json`, `claude logs <id>`, transcript | No |
| Agent teams | Experimental, off by default | Not in the feature table | Natural language to the team lead | Lead's agent panel; teammates' final answers; files under `~/.claude/teams` | n/a |
| `--session-id`, `--resume` | Documented, no preview label | All plans | UUID chosen at launch; resume by ID or name | Transcript JSONL; `claude -p --resume <id> --output-format json` (not for a running session) | n/a |
| Cross-session messaging (inbox socket) | No preview label; needs v2.1.224 or later | Subscription: yes. Same-machine on Console and cloud providers | Another session's SendMessage, or a script posting to `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` with `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN` | Reply via SendMessage to the sender, or transcript; same-machine traffic never goes through Anthropic servers | No |
| `statusline` `rate_limits` | Documented, no preview label | Pro, Max, Ultra only | Nothing: JSON on stdin at each update | Script stdout; a script may write files | n/a |
| `/usage` | Documented | Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise (plan bars and breakdown) | Typed command; runs while Claude responds; also from Remote Control | Terminal panel; no export documented | n/a |
| OAuth usage endpoint `/api/oauth/usage` | Undocumented | n/a | HTTP GET with a bearer token | JSON (third-party descriptions only) | n/a |

### 3.1 Channels

- **Research preview** (stated on the page). Requires claude.ai or Console API-key login.
- **Inbound:** an MCP server registered in `.mcp.json` and named with `--channels plugin:<name>@<marketplace>`. Events arrive as `<channel>` tags, and queue into the next turn. Anyone who can reply through a two-way channel can approve tool use, if the server declares the permission relay capability.
- **Outbound:** the reply tool. A notification gets no acknowledgement.
- **Custom channels:** not on the allowlist during preview, so they need `--dangerously-load-development-channels`, which is interactive-only. Under `-p` the flag is ignored.
- **Gating:** the org setting `channelsEnabled` and the sender allowlist apply.

### 3.2 Remote Control

- Requires a claude.ai login. The endpoint must be `api.anthropic.com`: a different `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` disables it. Zero Data Retention and HIPAA orgs cannot use it.
- One remote session per interactive process; server mode (`claude remote-control`) runs several.
- The session runs locally; the process must stay up. Transcripts are stored on Anthropic servers while connected.
- The docs describe a human-driven window. I found no documented API for a script to inject messages.
- Cross-session messaging can reach a Remote Control session on another machine, but only from a session that is itself connected to Remote Control.

### 3.3 Hooks

- Events include Stop, SubagentStop and Notification. The Notification matchers are permission_prompt, idle_prompt, agent_needs_input and agent_completed. The last two fire only while agent view is open.
- Stop and PostToolUse hooks use a top-level `decision: "block"`. The guide has a troubleshooting entry for a Stop hook hitting its block cap.
- Hooks are outbound: they can call a URL or run a command, but they cannot start a turn in another session.
- Hooks are listed as available on every provider.

### 3.4 Agent view and background sessions

- `claude --bg "prompt"` starts a session that runs without a terminal, under a supervisor (`claude daemon`). Each session uses the subscription independently.
- Inbound: a dispatch prompt in agent view starts a new session; a follow-up is a peek reply or `claude --resume <id> "prompt"`. The sessions doc says a piped or redirected run sends nothing and exits with status 1. So a script cannot reliably deliver a prompt this way.
- Outbound: `claude agents --json` for state; `claude logs <id>` for recent output; transcripts on disk.
- Sessions created with `-p` or the SDK are hidden from the picker and `--continue`, but resumable by ID.
- The entrypoint label of background sessions is not documented in what I read.

### 3.5 Agent teams

- Enabled by `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`. Experimental and off by default.
- Only the interactive lead spawns teammates; under `-p` or the SDK, Claude does not spawn them.
- Limitations: in-process teammates are not restored on `/resume`; one team per session; no nested teams.
- Input is natural language to the lead. There is no external entry point.

### 3.6 `--session-id` and `--resume`

- `--session-id <uuid>` pins the session ID at launch. `--resume` accepts an ID, a name or a transcript path.
- Resuming a running background session attaches to it. A prompt passed on the command line is sent as its next turn, after which the terminal attaches. Under `-p` with output flags, a running session is not opened and the command exits 1.
- This is the only documented way to re-enter a known session by ID. Whether the entrypoint of a resumed session changes is not documented.

### 3.7 Statusline `rate_limits`

- The JSON has `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage` (0 to 100) and `resets_at` (epoch seconds), and the same for `seven_day`.
- Present only for claude.ai Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers, and only after the first API response. Either window can be absent.
- The script runs on events, on window resets, or on `refreshInterval`. It uses no API tokens.
- A script can write the JSON to a file, which is a documented hook point but not a documented export.

### 3.8 `/usage`

- Shows plan bars and a breakdown by skill, subagent, plugin and MCP server. It can say the usage endpoint is rate limited and show last-known usage for up to 60 minutes.
- It is documented as a terminal panel. I found no documented way to script its output.

### 3.9 OAuth usage endpoint

- Not documented by Anthropic. Third-party sources describe `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with a Bearer OAuth token from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and the header `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`. One project reports a 403 “OAuth token does not meet scope requirement user:profile” for setup-tokens.
- Feature request #99231 says there is no supported way to read individual usage programmatically.
- Reusing Claude Code's OAuth token in your own tool falls in the area the Legal page restricts: developers “may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials.” That rule is aimed at products, so applying it to a personal script is a judgement call.

### 3.10 Cross-session messaging

- This is the only documented same-machine inbound path into a running interactive session from a script. Each session binds a per-session Unix socket (or a named pipe on Windows), exported as `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, with a token in `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`.
- Delivery: the receiving Claude reads the message between tool calls, or a new turn starts when the session is idle. The message is plain text, not a command, and it cannot approve permission prompts.
- Once delivered, it counts toward usage like a typed prompt.
- Default inbound handling depends on permission modes: a prompting receiver accepts by default; a bypassing receiver holds messages for approval. `crossSessionInbound: "accept"` in `--settings` lets a `-p` worker take messages unattended.
- Requires v2.1.224 or later (v2.1.234 on native Windows). Not reachable from Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry across machines.

### 3.11 stream-json `rate_limit_event`

- The Python SDK reference documents a `RateLimitEvent` emitted when status changes. The field path `rate_limit_info.unifiedWindows.five_hour.utilization` is reported by users from `-p` stream-json output and by an issue on another project. It is not in the pages I read.

## 4. Options closest to the documented line

- **API-key runs of `claude -p` or the SDK on Max, Ultra or Team:** monthly credits cover them, billed to the linked Console organization. Not Pro. Not interactive Claude Code.
- **Keep work in the interactive app on your own machine:** channels, hooks and cross-session messages are documented plan features. Their entrypoint labels are not documented, so check the `entrypoint` field in the transcript.
- **Cloud sessions and cloud scheduled tasks** are listed as available on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team. They run on Anthropic's cloud, not your machine.
- **Measure before you rely on a route:** `statusline` `rate_limits` or the `rate_limit_event` stream gives utilization; the transcript gives the label.

## 5. What stays uncertain

- **Staff replies to #97074:** the 72 items I could not load may contain one.
- **CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT:** official status depends on the `CLAUDE_CODE_E…` entries I did not read.
- **Whether the entrypoint label drives metering** is supported only by user measurements on one to three accounts each. No Anthropic confirmation.
- **Labels of channels, Remote Control, background sessions and cross-session messages:** undocumented. They matter for #97074.
- **Section 3 of the consumer terms** for US users (not read), and what “explicitly permit” covers beyond the help-center text.
- **The Nov 12 clause:** the in-force text before Nov 12 is known only through a tracker. Whether it will reach relabeling or personal scripts is unknown.
- **Agent view and agent teams:** I found no plan-availability list for either.
- **Changelog:** I read only part of the release notes.
- **Policy stability:** the June 15 pause and the Oct 7 credits show the terms have changed twice this year.
